newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 11/12 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 11/12 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money softened to 11.0/12.0 percent in early trading on Monday from 12/13 percent at the opening on sufficient liquidity supply, dealers said.
They said liquidity was sufficient despite a neutral central bank money policy on Monday.
One local bank dealer said call money rate was likely to rise on increasing demand ahead of the month-end factor and half-year book closing.
"Banks are now required to publish their reports only twice a year, not four times as previously required. They have only two opportunities to show their best," the bank dealer said.
The central bank offered one-week bilateral SBIs at 6.5 percent, two-week at 8.25, one-month at 10.25, three-month at 10.75, six-month at 11.5 and one-year at 12.0 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Friday was 14.91 percent compared with 8.48 percent on Thursday.
